title: Unconditional decidability of exact time-bounded CTMDP reachability
formal: Is there an unconditional algorithm that, for every finite rational-rate CTMDP with a designated absorbing state good, rational deadline \(T>0\) and rational threshold vector r, decides whether \(\sup _{\pi} \Pr _{s}^{\pi}\)[reach good by T]>\(r_{s}\) for every non-target state s, with timed positional policies as defined below?
definitions: The input lists a finite state set \(S=\{1,\ldots ,n\}\cup\){good}, \(n\ge 1; a\) nonempty finite action set \(A_{s}\) for each state; nonnegative rational rates \(q(s,a,t)\) for \(t\ne s; T\in Q_{>0}\); and \(r\in ([0,1]\cap Q)^{n}\). Integers and rational numerators/positive denominators are binary encoded. All rates out of good are zero, and the diagonal generator entry is \(q(s,a,s)=- \sum_{t\ne s}q(s,a,t)\). A decision vector d chooses one action \(d(s)\in A_{s}\) at each state. A policy is a Lebesgue-measurable map \(\pi :[0,T]\to \prod _{s} A_{s}\): at elapsed time u in state s the instantaneous generator row is \(q(s,\pi (u)(s),\cdot )\). Actions may change while the process remains in the same state, not only at jumps. Policies are deterministic and may depend on time and current state, with no computability restriction. For a fixed policy and initial state s, its probability law is the finite-state inhomogeneous Markov jump law with this bounded measurable generator. Equivalently its row distribution \(\rho _{s}(u)\) is the unique absolutely continuous solution of \(\rho _{s}(0)=e_{s}\) and \(\rho _{s}' (u)=\rho _{s}(u)Q^{\pi (u)}\) for almost every u. Bounded rates ensure nonexplosion. Since good is absorbing, the probability of reaching it at some time in \([0,T]\) equals \(\rho _{s}(T)_{\mathrm{good}}\). The supremum is taken over all such policies separately for each initial state. This defines the value without an attainment assumption; the source also proves existence of an optimal piecewise-constant timed positional policy. The decision uses strict > in every coordinate, so equality to any threshold requires NO. The algorithm is a deterministic Turing machine that halts with the correct YES/NO result on every valid encoding; there is no requested complexity bound and no number-theoretic oracle or unproved premise. Invalid encodings may be rejected.

context_blocks.text: A continuous-time decision process combines random event times with choices that can vary with elapsed time. The question concerns exact comparison of the best probability of reaching a target before a deadline.

Majumdar, Salamati and Soudjani define the strict vector-threshold question and prove its decidability assuming Schanuel’s conjecture. Their result does not give an unconditional decision procedure, and numerical approximation alone does not decide equality at the threshold.

why: Settle a foundational exact-verification question for continuous-time controlled stochastic systems.
answer_criterion: Give a terminating exact decision procedure with an unconditional proof for the specified strict vector-threshold predicate, or prove this language undecidable. Additive approximations, a procedure that may fail to halt at equality, or a theorem conditional on Schanuel’s conjecture do not settle it.
